safe_adaptations: Source Arc owner is cloned at construction. Original source and snapshots safely survive caller/editor destruction; no self-reference or unsafe.

C malloc length becomes actual Vec capacity for blob charge. Metadata actual capacities are exposed and checked against count limits, without incorrectly charging them to the C blob-only history byte cap.
Shared AtomicUsize accounting owner follows every unique blob until its final piece/command/snapshot owner drops, including after the editor is destroyed.

All significant local Vec allocations pass fallible reserve and a disabled-by-default thread-local deterministic test gate. Accepted peer parsers/save services retain their accepted fallible contracts; only standard Arc control-block allocation is an infallible exception.

C boolean-only allocation/validation helpers become typed Results, surfacing OutOfMemory at significant-allocation failures instead of collapsing it into a syntax/name boolean. Frozen meaningful error assertions for malformed XML/name, bounds, duplicates, limits and stale handles are retained.

Borrowed C caches become a OnceLock-owned model/token/span cache per source state. Mutations invalidate it only after publication; ordinary commits do not materialize/reparse a full model. Returned-handle operations prebuild the same eventual cache before commit so allocation failure cannot reject after mutation.

Measured two-pass decode/text/path outputs allocate nothing after cache build and avoid partial writes. materialize_into retains C required-length reporting; snapshot materialize_into retains zero length on failure; path capacity failure reports complete required length instead of the C partial-prefix count.
History labels use the original static strings, removing String allocation while retaining the 64-byte label contract.

history_jump preflights intermediate descriptors and XML validation, then publishes the final cursor/state once; allocation failure preserves original source, cursor, handles and save flags instead of a partial multi-step jump.
C NULL pointer/invalid enum combinations are excluded by Rust references, owned values and enums; no shim or unsupported platform stub is introduced.

Save uses accepted source_save_noop and copies original diagnostic, exact AtomicFileReplaceError discriminant (0..7), renamed/file_synced/directory_synced flags before dropping the borrowed token result. OK OR renamed marks saved; Durability remains SaveFailed with renamed flag.
